```{r setup}
library(ggpubr)
library(knitr)

labels <- c(
  old = "2.4.7 weighted",
  unclustered = "2.4.7 ignoring clusters",
  fork = "fork weighted"
)

files <- sprintf("output/results_%s.csv", names(labels))
results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(files[file.exists(files)], read.csv))
results$label <- factor(labels[results$label], levels = labels)

# Adjusted CIs as reported by summary.zcurve() (same rule as compare.R)
results$ERR_covered_adj <- with(results,
  pmax(ERR_lower - .03, .025) <= true_ERR & pmin(ERR_upper + .03, 1) >= true_ERR)
results$EDR_covered_adj <- with(results,
  pmax(EDR_lower - .05, .05) <= true_EDR & pmin(EDR_upper + .05, 1) >= true_EDR)

# Per-cell summaries written by compare.R
summary <- read.csv("output/summary.csv")
summary$label <- factor(labels[summary$label], levels = labels)
summary$setting <- sprintf("power = %.2f, rho = %.2f", summary$power, summary$rho)
summary$design <- sprintf("%g/%g", summary$total_sig_k, summary$av_sig_k_per_a)

n_sims <- max(results$simulation)
```

*The simulation code, results and this write-up were generated by Claude (Anthropic's AI model, Claude Code), directed by Shaheed Azaad.*

This page summarises the simulations for [FBartos/zcurve#33](https://github.com/FBartos/zcurve/issues/33): `zcurve_clustered(method = "w")` overestimated ERR and EDR. The weighted EM multiplied each mixture component's log-density by the article weight before mixing the components, i.e. it used $\theta_k f_k(z)^{w}$ instead of $\left(\sum_k \theta_k f_k(z)\right)^{w}$. This flattens the component densities rather than down-weighting the observation, and pulls the mixture weights towards the high-power components.

## How to run

Run everything from `simulations/`:

```zsh
./run_all.sh all old unclustered fork   # every dataset, all versions
./run_all.sh                            # every dataset, fork only
./run_all.sh 36                         # quick check on the first 36 datasets, fork only
quarto render results.qmd               # rebuild results.html and README.md
```

`run_all.sh` regenerates `output/sim_data.rds` when `gen_data.R` has changed, installs the fork from the `fix-issue-33` branch of [shaheedazaad/zcurve](https://github.com/shaheedazaad/zcurve) into `../lib/fork` (so push changes to the fork first), fits the chosen versions and runs `compare.R`. By default only the fork is refitted; existing results for the other versions are kept and still compared. After changing `gen_data.R`, refit all versions so they use the same data.

Settings:

- **Number of simulations per scenario**: `n_sims` at the top of `gen_data.R`. The scenario grid (power mixtures, `rhos`, `total_sig_k`, `av_sig_k_per_a`) is set just below it.
- **Number of bootstraps per fit**: `n_boot` near the top of `fit.R`.

## Methods

Data are generated by `gen_data.R`. Each article has 1 + Poisson attempted tests, and z-scores within an article share an error term with correlation `rho`. Only significant z-scores are kept, and articles are added until the dataset reaches the target number of significant results. Each article draws its power with equal probability from a three-point mixture, {0.1, 0.3, 0.5} (mean 0.3) or {0.2, 0.5, 0.8} (mean 0.5), and all tests within an article share that power. The `power` setting refers to the mixture mean. The true ERR and EDR are averaged over this mixture across all attempted tests.

In these datasets cluster size is **informative**: high-power articles produce more significant z-scores, so the number of z-scores in an article depends on its power. Weighting each z-score by 1 / (number of z-scores in its article) then down-weights high-power articles, and the weighted fit estimates an article-level rather than a test-level ERR and EDR. To separate this from the bug, every dataset also has an **uninformative** copy in which the z-scores are shuffled across articles: each article keeps its number of z-scores, but that number no longer depends on power. The shuffling also removes the within-article correlation, so `rho` only affects the informative datasets. The true ERR and EDR are the same for both copies.

Each of the `r nrow(unique(summary[c("cluster_size", "power", "rho", "total_sig_k", "av_sig_k_per_a")]))` scenarios was simulated `r n_sims` times and fitted with `fit.R` (`n_boot` bootstraps as set in `fit.R`, 95% percentile intervals) by three versions:

- **2.4.7 weighted**: CRAN zcurve 2.4.7, `zcurve_clustered(method = "w")`.
- **2.4.7 ignoring clusters**: CRAN zcurve 2.4.7, `zcurve(method = "EM")` treating every z-score as independent.
- **fork weighted**: the fork, where `zcurve_clustered(method = "w")` keeps the component densities unweighted and applies each z-score's weight (1 / number of z-scores in its article) to its contribution to the log-likelihood and to the mixture-weight update. Its bootstrap resamples articles with replacement, keeping all of their z-scores and their original weights.

In 2.4.7, the weighted bootstrap resamples individual z-scores (keeping their weights), not articles, so its CIs ignore between-article variability.

Coverage is reported for two intervals. **Raw** is the 95% percentile bootstrap interval. **Adjusted** is the interval that `summary()` reports: the percentile interval widened by .03 for ERR and .05 for EDR, as proposed by Bartoš & Schimmack, bounded below by .025 (ERR) and .05 (EDR) and above by 1. The adjusted intervals are computed from the raw bounds, so no extra fitting is needed.

Two fork fits (datasets 2984 and 4682) failed in the full run because the parallel workers failed to start. They were refitted with the same code and seeds, and their rows replaced in `output/results_fork.csv`.

With `r n_sims` simulations per scenario, the Monte Carlo standard error of a 95% coverage estimate is about `r round(sqrt(0.95 * 0.05 / n_sims), 3)`.

## Overall

```{r overall}
overall <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(results, results[c("label", "cluster_size")], drop = TRUE), function(r) {
  data.frame(
    `Cluster size` = r$cluster_size[1],
    Version = r$label[1],
    Fits = nrow(r),
    Failed = sum(is.na(r$ERR)),
    `ERR bias` = mean(r$ERR - r$true_ERR, na.rm = TRUE),
    `ERR coverage` = mean(r$ERR_covered, na.rm = TRUE),
    `ERR adj. coverage` = mean(r$ERR_covered_adj, na.rm = TRUE),
    `ERR CI width` = mean(r$ERR_width, na.rm = TRUE),
    `EDR bias` = mean(r$EDR - r$true_EDR, na.rm = TRUE),
    `EDR coverage` = mean(r$EDR_covered, na.rm = TRUE),
    `EDR adj. coverage` = mean(r$EDR_covered_adj, na.rm = TRUE),
    `EDR CI width` = mean(r$EDR_width, na.rm = TRUE),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))
overall <- overall[order(overall$`Cluster size`, overall$Version), ]
kable(overall, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE)
```

## By scenario

Each column is one combination of power and within-article correlation, and each row one estimand and cluster size; the x-axis varies the dataset size and the average number of significant z-scores per article.

```{r plot-fun}
plot_metric <- function(metric, ylab, ref = NULL) {
  long <- rbind(
    data.frame(summary[c("label", "setting", "design", "cluster_size")], estimand = "ERR", value = summary[[paste0("ERR_", metric)]]),
    data.frame(summary[c("label", "setting", "design", "cluster_size")], estimand = "EDR", value = summary[[paste0("EDR_", metric)]])
  )
  long$row <- factor(paste(long$estimand, long$cluster_size, sep = ", "),
                     levels = c("ERR, informative", "ERR, uninformative", "EDR, informative", "EDR, uninformative"))

  p <- ggline(long, x = "design", y = "value", color = "label", group = "label",
              facet.by = c("row", "setting"), palette = "jco",
              xlab = "Significant z-scores (total / per article)", ylab = ylab) +
    labs(color = NULL)

  if (!is.null(ref)) p <- p + geom_hline(yintercept = ref, linetype = "dashed")
  p
}
```

### Coverage

```{r coverage, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
plot_metric("coverage", "95% CI coverage", ref = 0.95)
```

### Adjusted coverage

```{r coverage-adj, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
plot_metric("coverage_adj", "Adjusted 95% CI coverage", ref = 0.95)
```

### CI width

```{r width, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
plot_metric("width", "Mean 95% CI width")
```

### Bias

```{r bias, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
plot_metric("bias", "Mean bias (estimate - truth)", ref = 0)
```

### RMSE

```{r rmse, fig.width = 10, fig.height = 10}
plot_metric("rmse", "RMSE")
```
